claims.claim: The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084 'Origin of Light' (fetched 2026-11-17); Mitalas & Sills 1992, ApJ 401, 759 (NASA ADS scan, both pages read; Crossref confirms doi:10.1086/172103); NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (fetched)
claims.note: SVS: 'Over the course of 40,000 years it will be absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface' and 'Over tens of thousands of years, the photons travel a "drunken walk"'. M&S abstract: '1.7 x 10^5 yr for the diffusion time scale of the present Sun', taken as the time to reach the inner edge of the convective zone; they call the textbook 3x10^3-3x10^4 yr 'much too short'. MSFC: 'about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. A floor of tens of thousands holds for every source read. Even with M&S's eq. 2 factor of 3 (3<r^2> = N<l^2>, against <r^2> = N l^2 for an isotropic walk) removed, ~6e4 yr is still tens of thousands. 'Maybe far more' is covered by M&S (1.7e5) and MSFC (~1e6), so it does not rest on Stix, which was not read. Sources speak of a photon's diffusion. The script's 'energy' is the more careful framing of the same process, since SVS says the photon is absorbed and re-emitted.

claims.claim: A4: what a viewer who swipes at second two takes away
claims.note: By 2.05 s only 'The energy in the sunlight on your' has been spoken, and the screen shows the Sun, Earth labelled 'not to scale' and a pulse crossing the gap. Nothing false is asserted. The full first sentence (to ~6 s) claims only a floor of tens of thousands of years for the energy, which every source read supports (claim 1). It avoids the false popular form that the same photon is that old.

claims.claim: The trip from the Sun to you took eight minutes.
claims.source_checked: NIST CODATA 2022 c (physics.nist.gov Value?c: 299 792 458 m/s exact); NSSDC Sun fact sheet (radius 695,700 km; distance mean 149.6, min 147.1, max 152.1 x10^6 km); NSSDC Earth fact sheet (semimajor axis 149.598e6 km, e = 0.0167); NASA SVS 11084
claims.note: Photosphere to Earth: (149,597,870.7 - 695,700) km / c = 496.7 s = 8 min 17 s. Perihelion 8.14 min, aphelion 8.42 min. SVS: 'Light takes eight minutes to travel the 93 million miles from the sun to Earth.' 'Eight minutes' is a fair rounding. The IAU 2012 B2 text (exact AU) was not reachable, but NSSDC's 149.6e6 km gives the same 499 s, so nothing depends on it.

claims.claim: Getting out was the slow part.
claims.note: About 8 minutes against at least 4e4 years. No new figure.

claims.claim: But it is not the same light.
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084; NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'
claims.note: SVS: absorbed 'and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface'. MSFC: radiation inside is 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays', while the energy 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. Different light, both in kind and as individual photons. MSFC's 'an individual photon takes about a million years' reads as one photon, but the script does not lean on that wording.

claims.claim: Deep inside, it travels mostly as gamma rays and X-rays.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (temperatures and the phrase 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays'); NIST CODATA Wien displacement constant b = 2.897771955e-3 m K (physics.nist.gov Value?bwien)
claims.note: The words match MSFC, but A3 is not met. The SOURCES block (entry 4) records that the physics disagrees with MSFC and keeps the broader reading, while A3 requires the narrower claim when sources disagree. Using MSFC's own temperatures and the CODATA Wien constant, the thermal radiation peaks at about 6.4 keV (15 MK), 3.0 keV (7 MK) and 0.86 keV (2 MK): X-rays. At 15 MK, kT = 1.3 keV, so the blackbody share above ~100 keV is about e^-77, effectively zero. Gamma rays occur only as the fusion products MSFC names ('a helium-3 nucleus and a gamma ray'), which thermalise at once. A pedant will say there are essentially no gamma rays in the radiative zone. Change to 'Deep inside, it travels mostly as X-rays.' or 'It is born as gamma rays and crosses the Sun mostly as X-rays.' Source entry 4 to MSFC plus the Wien calculation, and update the keyPhrases ['gamma','rays'], the F.photon anchor edit.at('gamma') in index.tsx and the same sentence in the description (claim 25).

claims.claim: It leaves as sunlight.
claims.note: MSFC: 'These reactions release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light.'

claims.claim: The energy is ancient.
claims.note: Rests on the ≥4e4-year floor in claim 1. 'Ancient' is a fair word for that.

claims.claim: Its last eight minutes were the trip to you.
claims.note: The same 8.1-8.4 min photosphere-to-Earth figure, and SVS 'Light takes eight minutes'.

claims.claim: Sun-Earth shot: Earth labelled 'not to scale' while visible, a bright pulse crossing the gap
claims.source_checked: src/shorts/age-of-sunlight/index.tsx (earth opacity and label share the same condition, earth > 0)
claims.note: Earth is drawn far too big and close, and the pulse crosses in ~3 s. Both are covered by the 'not to scale' label, which is shown whenever Earth is (A6).

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES / surface to your skin / not to scale
claims.note: Photosphere to Earth is 8.1-8.4 min. 'Surface' matches the computation from the photosphere.

claims.claim: 10,000+ YEARS / energy, core to surface / not to scale
claims.source_checked: as claim 1; MSFC on the convection zone; M&S section 3
claims.note: Every source read is at or above 4e4 yr, so '10,000+' is a safe floor and does not contradict the spoken 'tens of thousands'. M&S and MSFC measure to the base of the convection zone. Core to surface adds only the convective crossing, which MSFC calls 'quite rapidly' and M&S 'very much shorter'. SVS's 40,000 is explicitly to the surface.

claims.claim: THE ENERGY / 10,000+ years getting out
claims.note: Same floor as claim 12.

claims.claim: THE TRIP / 8 minutes to you / not to scale
claims.note: Same as claim 11.

claims.claim: Cutaway rings at 0.25 and 0.7 of the Sun's radius (core, radiative zone)
claims.note: MSFC: core is 'the innermost 25%' ('175,000 km from the center'); the radiative zone runs 'from 25% ... to 70%'; the convection zone is 'the outermost 30%', from a depth of ~200,000 km (0.71 R). The 0.713 R of Christensen-Dalsgaard, Gough & Thompson 1991 was checked only on Crossref (title 'The depth of the solar convection zone'), not read. Nothing shown depends on it.

claims.claim: A random-walk path from the centre to the 0.7 ring, with short sideways strokes along it
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084; Mitalas & Sills 1992; NASA MSFC
claims.note: SVS: 'drunken walk, zigzagging from atom to atom', 'absorbed ... and emitted repeatedly'. M&S define the diffusion time from centre to the inner edge of the convective zone, which matches the path's start and end. The sideways strokes stand for re-emission in other directions. It is labelled not to scale, since M&S's 0.090 cm step cannot be drawn.

claims.claim: Path coloured violet toward pale yellow by log temperature (15 MK at r=0, 7 MK at 0.25 R, 2 MK at 0.7 R, 5,700 K at the surface; ~10% to yellow at 0.25 R, ~26% at 0.7 R)
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; recomputed the mapping
claims.note: MSFC: centre 'about 15,000,000° C'; the radiative zone falls 'from 7,000,000° C to about 2,000,000° C'; surface '5,700 K'. ln(15e6/7e6)/ln(15e6/5700) = 0.097 and ln(15e6/2e6)/ln(15e6/5700) = 0.256, which matches the brief. No number or wavelength label is on screen. The hue is schematic and runs from high-energy toward visible, consistent with the physics, so it does not depend on the gamma/X-ray wording in claim 6.

claims.claim: Rotating dashed convection cells between 0.7 and the surface
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; Mitalas & Sills 1992 section 3
claims.note: MSFC: energy moves 'by convective fluid flows (boiling motion) through the convection zone, the outermost 30%'. In the code the cells span roughly 0.73-0.97 R.

claims.claim: A fan of five yellow rays leaving the surface
claims.note: MSFC: the energy 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'.

claims.claim: The energy in sunlight took tens of thousands of years to get out of the Sun
claims.note: The title drops the spoken hedge 'maybe far more', which turns a floor into a magnitude. The best peer-reviewed source gives 1.7x10^5 yr (hundreds of thousands) and MSFC gives about a million, so the title changes the claim (A3/E2). Change to 'The energy in sunlight took at least tens of thousands of years to get out of the Sun' (or '...tens of thousands of years or more...'). The same string is the `title` in src/shorts/age-of-sunlight/index.tsx.

claims.claim: Sunlight reaches you about eight minutes after leaving the Sun's surface.
claims.note: 8.1-8.4 min from the photosphere.

claims.claim: But the energy it carries spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out.
claims.note: Same as the spoken hook.

claims.claim: Published estimates run from about 40,000 years (NASA SVS) through 170,000 (Mitalas & Sills 1992) to about a million (NASA Marshall).
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084; Mitalas & Sills 1992 (scan); NASA MSFC
claims.note: Each attributed figure is right: SVS 40,000; M&S 1.7x10^5; MSFC 'about a million'. 'Run from ... to' claims this is the full published range, and that is false. M&S quote published textbook estimates of 3x10^3-3x10^4 yr (Shu 1982, Bahcall 1989 and others), and Stix 2003, listed in this same description, argues for far longer (~3e7 yr per SOURCES; not read). Change to 'Estimates include about 40,000 years (NASA SVS), 170,000 (Mitalas & Sills 1992) and about a million (NASA Marshall).'

claims.claim: The slow part is the crawl through the Sun's radiative zone; convection then carries it quickly to the surface.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; Mitalas & Sills 1992 section 3
claims.note: MSFC: 'about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'; 'These convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface.' M&S: 'the crossing time of the convective zone by convecting elements is very much shorter than the time for the photon ... to reach the inner edge of the convective zone'.

claims.claim: Deep inside, it travels mostly as gamma rays and X-rays. It leaves as sunlight.
claims.note: Same problem as claim 6. Change it in step with the spoken line, for example 'Deep inside, it travels mostly as X-rays. It leaves as sunlight.' The 'It leaves as sunlight' part is confirmed (MSFC).

claims.claim: Illustrated animation; marked shots are not to scale.
claims.note: The Sun-Earth shot carries 'not to scale' on Earth, and on the 8 MINUTES and THE TRIP tags. The cutaway is covered by the '10,000+ YEARS ... not to scale' tag for as long as it is up (F.rest to F.ancient+48, and the cutaway fades by F.ancient+48).
